name: Michael Darmousseh
current_role: Co-founder, Extend (product-protection/warranty platform, San Francisco); listed variously as SVP Engineering / CTO
profile: Co-founder of Extend, the San Francisco post-purchase platform offering product protection, shipping protection and returns for merchants. He started the company in February 2019 with Woodrow Levin, Joe Moss and Rohan Shah; Extend raised a $260M SoftBank-led round in 2021 at a valuation of over $1B.
interesting_fact: Extend was co-founded in February 2019 and within ten months of its Series A closed a $40M Series B, signing merchants such as Peloton, iRobot and Harman/JBL.
notes: Low public profile; engineering-side co-founder. Exact current title unverified (sources say SVP Engineering, CTO or Distinguished Engineer). Best route likely via Extend (extend.com) or CEO Woodrow Levin. No published press email found.

name: Huang Yun
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Shenzhen Shunfeng Express Co. (SF Freight / 顺丰快运), per 36Kr company record (may be dated)
profile: Huang Yun (黄贇) is listed as chairman and legal representative of SF Freight (顺丰快运), the less-than-truckload and heavy-parcel freight arm of China's SF Holding group, incorporated in Shenzhen in October 2019. SF Freight raised a US$300M round in 2020 from CCP, CDH and Legend Capital, among others. Little else is publicly documented about him.
interesting_fact: SF Freight's company entity was set up on 9 Oct 2019 and raised a US$300M round in Feb 2020 from investors including CDH Investments and Legend Capital.
notes: Very low public profile; Chinese name appears as 黄贇 in the 36Kr registry entry. 'Founder' framing comes from Hurun; he is better described as SF Freight's chairman within SF Holding (founded by Wang Wei). Current role after ~2020 not verified. Route would be via SF Holding investor/press relations.

name: Ilan Atias
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Melio (B2B payments; acquired by Xero in 2025) - current status post-acquisition unverified
profile: Israeli engineer who co-founded Melio in 2018 with Matan Bar and others, serving as CTO and running its Tel Aviv R&D centre. Melio, a bill-pay platform for US small businesses, was acquired by New Zealand's Xero for about $2.5B, completing in October 2025.
interesting_fact: When Melio hired an R&D chief in 2022, Atias said platform processing volume was 'surging to tens of billions of dollars annually'; Xero later bought Melio for about $2.5B.
notes: Search snippets suggest he may have left Melio after the Xero deal (unverified). Prior role reportedly VP R&D at maritime-AI firm Windward (aggregator sources only, not verified).

name: Marek Sacha
current_role: Co-founder of Cera (UK home care); later head of XOM Materials (Klöckner-backed materials e-commerce platform) - current title unverified
profile: Czech-British entrepreneur (b. 1987), ex-McKinsey consultant, who was the first CEO of Czech online grocer Rohlik.cz and in 2015 co-founded Cera Care, the London tech-enabled home-care company, with Ben Maruthappu and Martin Ocenas, leading it until 2018. He then joined XOM Materials, a digital materials-trading platform initiated by Klöckner.
interesting_fact: Before Cera he was the first CEO of Rohlik.cz, the Czech online supermarket founded by Tomáš Čupr in 2014; Forbes Czech named him to its 30 Under 30 in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He was formerly a competitive basketball player, and describes his focus as 'overlooked opportunities in boring or complicated industries from healthcare to groceries' (Aspen Young Leaders Program 2017 bio).
notes: Left Cera's leadership in 2018; Cera is now led by Ben Maruthappu. Aspen bio (2017) also lists him as CEO of Benefio, a family VC firm. No published personal contact found.

name: Sandeep Kella
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman of the Board, Pacvue (since Sept 2024; previously CEO)
profile: Co-founder and former CEO of Assembly, an e-commerce software roll-up that bought Amazon-seller tool Helium 10 (2020) and enterprise retail-media platform Pacvue (2021), then took the Pacvue name. In September 2024 he handed the CEO role to Rahul Choraria and became executive chairman, overseeing strategy.
interesting_fact: He bought Pacvue just one month after an Advent International-led round pushed Assembly's valuation above $1B; Pacvue says revenue quadrupled in four years and it has been 'highly profitable since inception'.
deep_cut_fact: When he stepped up to executive chairman in 2024 he brought onto Pacvue's board Harry Shum, the computer scientist who led Microsoft's AI and Research group.
notes: Acquirer/operator rather than original Pacvue founder (Pacvue was founded by Melissa Burdick and others; Kella co-founded Assembly). Low media profile.

name: James Carter
current_role: Co-founder, Gousto (UK recipe-box company); current role at the company not verified
profile: British entrepreneur who co-founded Gousto, the London meal-kit/recipe-box business, with Timo Boldt in 2012. Gousto reached unicorn status in 2021. Carter keeps a low public profile and Boldt has been the public face as CEO.
interesting_fact: Carter and Boldt pitched Gousto on BBC's Dragons' Den in 2013 and left without a deal, yet Gousto went on to become a unicorn in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Within weeks of walking away empty-handed from Dragons' Den, he and Boldt closed a £500,000 investment from food-industry players, plus $300,000 from ex-BSkyB MD Ian West and Rothschild vice-chairman Andrea Raffel; both founders were 29 and made the Startups 'Young Guns' class of 2014.
notes: Common name - use 'Gousto co-founder' to disambiguate. No public contact found for him; route via Gousto press office. Note Startups.co.uk misnames Boldt as 'Timo Schmidt'. Whether Carter is still at Gousto is unverified.

name: Teddy Cross
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Playco (Tokyo-based instant-play games company)
profile: American game producer and engineer and early HTML5 gaming pioneer who worked with Michael Carter at Game Closure from 2011 and led software development at tech companies in Korea. In 2020 he co-founded Playco with Carter, Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and ex-DeNA executive Takeshi Otsuka; it debuted as a unicorn with a $100M Series A.
interesting_fact: Playco launched in Sept 2020 already a unicorn: a $100M Series A at just over $1B valuation, co-led by Josh Buckley and Sequoia Capital Global Equities, with backers including Keisuke Honda's KSK Angel Fund.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 2011 at age 15 as a software intern in gaming, building HTML5 puzzle games that quickly gained thousands of users, and later became a well-known figure in the Korean tech scene.
notes: website@play.co is Playco's published general-inquiry address (not personal). Very young founder (born c.1996 per Playco bio age).

name: Deng Guobiao
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, XTransfer (Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments platform for SMEs)
profile: Deng Guobiao ('Bill Deng') spent over a decade in payments, first at Visa and then at Ant Financial's Alipay (joined 2010), before co-founding XTransfer in May 2017 with five former Alibaba/Ant colleagues as a 'B2B version of Alipay'. XTransfer serves 800,000+ enterprises and holds payment licences in multiple markets; he now speaks widely on stablecoins for trade.
interesting_fact: Deng says he jumped to found XTransfer after watching colleagues leave to start businesses including ride-hailing giant Didi; he argues stablecoins suit cross-border B2B trade because 'when it comes to money, there's no 24/7 infrastructure'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alipay he worked at Visa; Alibaba's eWTP fund led XTransfer's $15M Series B1, and Deng has said 'Our background from Alibaba indeed offers a good start'.
notes: Goes by Bill Deng in English media; active conference speaker (Singapore FinTech Festival, Forum Ekonomi Malaysia). No dedicated press email found; contact page offers general inquiry form.

name: Dileep Thazhmon
current_role: Founder and CEO, Jeeves (global corporate card, spend management and cross-border business finance platform)
profile: Serial entrepreneur and Stanford GSB graduate who co-founded and ran ad-tech firm PowerInbox (later Jeeng) as COO before founding Jeeves (Y Combinator S20). Jeeves offers multi-currency corporate cards, payments and credit to companies across Latin America, Europe and North America; it raised $180M led by Tencent at a $2.1B valuation in March 2022.
interesting_fact: Jeeves hit a $2.1B valuation only about seven months after its $57M Series B, in a Tencent-led $180M Series C that included Stanford University and GIC as investors.
deep_cut_fact: At PowerInbox, an email ad server used by 600+ brands including CNN and Disney, he grew the team from 3 to 50+ while keeping it profitable at $35M+ ARR; it ranked #3 on Deloitte's Fast50. He also worked in venture capital earlier.
notes: Featured on HubSpot for Startups 'Spiraling Up: The Journey to Become a Unicorn' (S1 ep3), where he calls Jeeves his 'legacy project' - good podcast hook. No published press email found for Jeeves.

name: Deepika Bodapati
current_role: Co-founder of Athelas; COO of Commure (Athelas merged with Commure in Oct 2023)
profile: Co-founded Athelas with Tanay Tandon (Y Combinator), building the Athelas One, an FDA-cleared, internet-connected finger-prick device that measures white blood cell and neutrophil counts at home, and expanding into remote patient monitoring and revenue-cycle software. After Athelas merged with healthcare infrastructure firm Commure in 2023 she became COO of the combined company.
interesting_fact: Athelas One became key for schizophrenia patients on clozapine, who need regular white-cell monitoring; the work led to a partnership with clozapine maker HLS Therapeutics and deployments in California state hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Even as Athelas neared unicorn status she personally read every customer support ticket; persistent emails from Dr. Deanna Kelly of the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center led Bodapati to call her, opening the clozapine use case.
notes: Route via Commure/Athelas. No published press email found in this session.

name: Gady Shlasky
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO/President of Optibus (transit-planning software); no longer with the company - current role unknown
profile: Israeli co-founder of Optibus, the AI-driven public-transport planning and scheduling platform founded in 2011 with Amos Haggiag (now CEO) and Eitan Yanovsky. Shlasky was the company's early CEO, selling real-time bus rescheduling to operators such as Egged; Hurun lists Optibus as a $1B unicorn. Directory sources say he has since left the company.
interesting_fact: In 2014, as Optibus CEO, he said the startup already managed about 60% of Israel's bus schedules and could save operators 7-10% a year by reassigning buses in real time, helping them avoid municipal fines of up to NIS 10,000 for running late.
deep_cut_fact: Early on, Optibus was enrolled in IBM's Alpha Zone accelerator and named one of seven finalists in Ernst & Young's 'The Pitch' contest; Shlasky flagged airlines as a possible long-term market beyond buses.
notes: Left Optibus (per directory sources); current venture not verified. Optibus general contact info@optibus.com is published on optibus.com but is a company address, not his. Has a LinkedIn (il.linkedin.com/in/gadyshlasky) - not verified as active.

name: Frank Wolf
current_role: Co-founder, Staffbase (Chemnitz-based employee communications platform); listed as President & Co-Founder on recruiter profiles - current title unverified
profile: German entrepreneur who spent years as a consultant building enterprise intranets before co-founding Staffbase in Chemnitz in 2014 with Martin Böhringer and Lutz Gerlach. Staffbase launched what it calls the world's first employee app and now serves 1,500 customers and 16.5M users; it is still founder-led and was valued at over €1B (OMR, 2022).
interesting_fact: Staffbase's founding idea came from Wolf's frustration that the big enterprise intranets he built as a consultant were complex, expensive and used by only a fraction of the workforce - so they designed for 'the hardest-to-reach employee'.
deep_cut_fact: Wolf championed Dresden as Staffbase's 'kind of second headquarters', moving there largely to recruit software talent from TU Dresden; by end-2020 the Dresden office had 62 staff.
notes: Staffbase is headquartered in Chemnitz, East Germany - a notable non-Berlin unicorn story. CEO is Martin Böhringer; Wolf is lower-profile.

name: Jeff Smedsrud
current_role: Founder & CEO, Pivot Health (short-term/supplemental health insurance products, now part of HealthCare.com); co-founder of HealthCare.com
profile: Health-insurance marketing veteran who co-founded HealthCare.com, the health-coverage shopping and lead-generation company (Hurun lists it at a $1B valuation), and founded Pivot Health, an Arizona-based designer and marketer of short-term and supplemental health plans that HealthCare.com later acquired. Pivot Health products are sold through HealthCare.com sites such as Healthcare Insider.
interesting_fact: HealthCare.com both publishes consumer guides (e.g. Healthcare Insider) and manufactures its own short-term and supplemental health insurance products under the Pivot Health brand that Smedsrud founded.
notes: Low public profile; ThinkAdvisor ran a 2022 profile 'The View From HealthCare.com: Jeff Smedsrud' (paywalled/blocked, not read). pivothealth.com now redirects to healthcare.com/about-company. No press email found.

name: Sean Hunt
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Solugen (Houston chemicals company using enzymes + metal catalysis - 'Bioforge' plants)
profile: MIT chemical engineer (SM '13, PhD '16) who co-founded Solugen in 2016 with physician-scientist Gaurab Chakrabarti. Solugen makes hydrogen peroxide and other commodity chemicals from sugar using engineered enzymes and metal catalysts instead of petrochemicals; Hunt leads the chemienzymatic process technology behind its Bioforge plants. Forbes 30 Under 30.
interesting_fact: Solugen's first lab was leased for $150/month near the Houston airport in a facility TechCrunch said made it possibly 'the first legitimate multi-million-dollar company to start out in a meth lab'; Chakrabarti calls himself 'the Heisenberg of hydrogen peroxide'.
deep_cut_fact: Their first customers were float-spa owners: one saw the MIT $100K pitch video and shared it in a Facebook group of ~400 US float spas. Hunt then spent $7,000 at Home Depot building a pilot reactor - 'this little PVC bubble column' - and fed it 55-gallon drums of sugar. He calls himself a 'recovering biotech skeptic'.
notes: Great fit for energy/industrial podcast: Solugen now pitches its Forges as dual-use for energy systems and defense. Hunt has appeared on podcasts (e.g. MCJ 'Inevitable' ep.175 with Chakrabarti, The Chemical Show).

name: Andrew Busey
current_role: Co-founder, Colossal Biosciences (de-extinction) and Form Bio (Colossal software spin-out; co-CEO at 2022 spin-out, later reportedly executive chair - current title unverified)
profile: Austin-based software entrepreneur who co-founded Colossal Biosciences, the de-extinction company behind the woolly mammoth and thylacine projects, serving as chief product officer. In 2022 he and Kent Wakeford spun out Form Bio, a computational life-sciences software platform, with $30M in funding, and he became its co-CEO.
interesting_fact: At Colossal he led the Austin software effort to build a standardized way of using and sharing genomic data, which became the basis for the Form Bio spin-out.
deep_cut_fact: Besides building software companies, he is an occasional science-fiction novelist, as the Austin Chronicle noted in its 2022 Colossal feature.
notes: Earlier ventures reportedly include social-games startups sold to Zynga and chatbot company Conversable (acquired by LivePerson) - aggregator sources only, not verified. Duke entrepreneurship alumni profile exists (andrew-busey-93).

name: Shen Haifa
current_role: Co-founder & former CTO of StemiRna Therapeutics (斯微生物); per a BIO convention speaker bio, now CEO & co-founder of MicroX Pharmaceutics (mRNA delivery) - not independently confirmed
profile: Drug-delivery scientist (沈海法) who co-founded Shanghai mRNA company StemiRna Therapeutics in 2016 with Li Hangwen, serving as CTO and holding ~11.9% at founding. StemiRna was one of China's earliest mRNA players and a lead mRNA COVID-19 vaccine developer. Shen was previously a nanomedicine researcher at Houston Methodist Research Institute with a Weill Cornell appointment.
interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing the Lipopolyplex (LPP) mRNA delivery platform, which has been used to develop multiple clinical-stage products.
deep_cut_fact: Before moving into industry he was founding director of the Innovative Therapeutics Program at the Houston Methodist Cancer Center and a professor of nanomedicine at Weill Cornell Medicine.
notes: StemiRna has been in financial and governance difficulties since 2022 (avoid in outreach). Founding shareholding and CTO title from 36Kr registry page: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678467395941379. BIO speaker page returned 404 on direct fetch; its content was seen only via search snippets.

name: Nathaniel Bennett
current_role: Co-founder, Xaira Therapeutics (AI drug discovery; South San Francisco/Seattle) - employed there per 2025 Nature paper disclosures
profile: Protein-design scientist (Nate Bennett, PhD) trained at the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design under Nobel laureate David Baker, where he worked on generative deep-learning models for designing binding proteins, including RFdiffusion. He co-founded Xaira Therapeutics with Baker and Joseph Watson; Xaira launched in 2024 with over $1B in funding and licenses IPD technology.
interesting_fact: He was co-lead author of the 2025 Nature paper 'Atomically accurate de novo design of antibodies with RFdiffusion' - AI-designed antibodies created from scratch - technology Xaira has licensed.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining why de novo antibodies matter, he noted that many diseases have no approved medicines because they are driven by molecules with vulnerable sites that small-molecule drugs can't reach - 'Computer-generated antibodies could target these sites directly.' The RFantibody code was released openly on GitHub.
notes: Scientist-founder rather than the business lead (Xaira launched with ex-Genentech executives in leadership, per BioSpace headline). info@xaira.com is the company's general contact.

name: Phil Beahon
current_role: Co-founder (and co-CEO alongside brother Tom), Castore - British premium sportswear brand
profile: Former county cricketer who co-founded Castore with his brother Tom Beahon in 2015, when he was just 22. The premium sportswear brand now kits major teams and athletes - from Rangers, Newcastle and McLaren F1 to Andy Murray and Adam Peaty - positioning itself as a British challenger to Nike, Adidas and Puma.
interesting_fact: Castore was founded when Tom was 25 and Phil only 22; within six years it was supplying Andy Murray, Owen Farrell, Adam Peaty, McLaren F1 and the West Indies cricket team.
deep_cut_fact: Before Castore he racked up caps for Cheshire and Lancashire in county cricket - and in March 2025 Castore signed a multi-year kit deal with Lancashire Cricket, his former county.
notes: Tom Beahon tends to be the brothers' public voice. No published press email found for Castore in this session; route via Castore's corporate/PR team or LinkedIn.

name: Brian Menell
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, TechMet Ltd (Dublin/London critical-minerals investment company)
profile: Johannesburg-born (1965) mining executive and grandson of Anglovaal co-founder Slip Menell. After eight years at De Beers he ran Anglovaal Mining with his brother until its 2001 sale formed African Rainbow Minerals. In 2017 he founded TechMet, which invests in mining, processing and recycling of lithium, nickel, cobalt, tin, tungsten and rare earths; it launched TechMet USA in 2026.
interesting_fact: While at Anglovaal he was a 50% partner in the Venetia diamond mine; De Beers' $600M purchase of Anglovaal's stake was the largest acquisition in De Beers' history.
deep_cut_fact: He started at De Beers as a diamond sorter (working in London, Antwerp and Windhoek), and in 2004 was a founding partner and executive director of the A1 Grand Prix auto racing series.
notes: Very strong fit for an energy podcast: frequent media/podcast guest on critical minerals (e.g. SmarterMarkets at FT Commodities Global Summit 2026, Mining Indaba). Reuters (Feb 2026): TechMet seeking up to $200M more after raising $300M incl. $180M from QIA.
